decisions.statement: A name is read from its slug.
A slug never has a dot.
The page type follows the slug.
A list of sections follows the page type.
The last part is the form the file has.
A page's name is the slug and the page type parted by a dot.
Whether the page type slot names a page type is answered against the set handed in.
Whether a name is shaped as a page's is answered without any set of page types.
A name shaped that way carries a slug, a page type and `ts` and nothing between.
Whether a section names a file property is answered against the set handed in.
A section list is a property slug or a group slug and then a member slug.
A group member's key is the group slug and the member slug joined by a dot.
A section list of two is read only where the set handed in has that key.
A name carrying a known page type but held as anything but TypeScript is no page.
The form a property's file has is read as written.
A page and a file beside the page answer the same page.
The name a property's file is under is built here as well as read here.
The name `heldIn` takes apart and the name the builders here put together stay one rule.
Whether the sections past a page's name are a property's is answered here.
A path that is no TypeScript file is refused rather than answered.
The section `uncommitted` is reserved.
A file whose only section is `uncommitted` has the uncommitted values of that file's page.
A file whose only section is `uncommitted` is never a property's file nor a page.
A section list may end in `uncommitted`.
A file whose section list ends in `uncommitted` has a property that is not committed.
The section `sops` is reserved.
A file whose only section is `sops` has the secret values of that file's page.
A file whose only section is `sops` is never a property's file nor a page.
One sops file has every secret a page has.
A page's sops file is the name that sops file is already under.
A file property slug is never a reserved section.
A part section is the word `part` and a part number.
The least part number is two.
A part section follows the property slug and precedes `uncommitted`.
The first of a property's files has no part section.
A reserved section has no part.
A file git leaves out of the commit spells `uncommitted` between two dots.
That spelling is read from the name alone, whatever else the name is.
Nothing here reads the index or the disk.

definition: what a file's name says about the page it has or sits beside
